requirements.quote:
The header fields in PUSH_PROMISE and any subsequent CONTINUATION
   frames MUST be a valid and complete set of request header fields
   (Section 8.3.1).  The server MUST include a method in the ":method"
   pseudo-header field that is safe and cacheable.  If a client receives
   a PUSH_PROMISE that does not include a complete and valid set of
   header fields or the ":method" pseudo-header field identifies a
   method that is not safe, it MUST respond on the promised stream with
   a stream error (Section 5.4.2) of type PROTOCOL_ERROR.
requirements.condition: When a server sends a PUSH_PROMISE and any subsequent CONTINUATION frames.
requirements.required_behavior: The contained header fields must form a valid and complete set of request header fields.
requirements.why_checkable: The decoded field block can be checked for validity and completeness as a request header set.

requirements.quote:
The header fields in PUSH_PROMISE and any subsequent CONTINUATION
   frames MUST be a valid and complete set of request header fields
   (Section 8.3.1).  The server MUST include a method in the ":method"
   pseudo-header field that is safe and cacheable.  If a client receives

   header fields or the ":method" pseudo-header field identifies a
   method that is not safe, it MUST respond on the promised stream with

requirements.condition: When a server sends a PUSH_PROMISE.
requirements.required_behavior: The server must include a method in the ":method" pseudo-header field.
requirements.why_checkable: The PUSH_PROMISE field block can be inspected for presence of the ":method" pseudo-header field and a method value.

requirements.quote:
The header fields in PUSH_PROMISE and any subsequent CONTINUATION
   frames MUST be a valid and complete set of request header fields

requirements.condition: When a server includes a method in a PUSH_PROMISE ":method" pseudo-header field.
requirements.required_behavior: The identified method must be safe.
requirements.why_checkable: The method value can be classified as safe and compared with the requirement.

requirements.why_checkable: The method value can be classified as cacheable and compared with the requirement.

requirements.quote:
The header fields in PUSH_PROMISE and any subsequent CONTINUATION
   frames MUST be a valid and complete set of request header fields
   (Section 8.3.1).  The server MUST include a method in the ":method"
   pseudo-header field that is safe and cacheable.  If a client receives
   a PUSH_PROMISE that does not include a complete and valid set of
   header fields or the ":method" pseudo-header field identifies a
   method that is not safe, it MUST respond on the promised stream with

requirements.condition: If a client receives a PUSH_PROMISE without a complete and valid set of header fields.
requirements.error_behavior: The client must respond on the promised stream with a stream error of type PROTOCOL_ERROR.
requirements.why_checkable: A malformed or incomplete PUSH_PROMISE can be injected and the promised stream response checked for PROTOCOL_ERROR.

requirements.quote:
The header fields in PUSH_PROMISE and any subsequent CONTINUATION
   frames MUST be a valid and complete set of request header fields
   (Section 8.3.1).  The server MUST include a method in the ":method"
   pseudo-header field that is safe and cacheable.  If a client receives
   a PUSH_PROMISE that does not include a complete and valid set of
   header fields or the ":method" pseudo-header field identifies a
   method that is not safe, it MUST respond on the promised stream with
   a stream error (Section 5.4.2) of type PROTOCOL_ERROR.
requirements.condition: If a client receives a PUSH_PROMISE whose ":method" pseudo-header field identifies an unsafe method.
requirements.error_behavior: The client must respond on the promised stream with a stream error of type PROTOCOL_ERROR.
requirements.why_checkable: A PUSH_PROMISE identifying an unsafe method can be injected and the promised stream response checked for PROTOCOL_ERROR.

requirements.quote:
The server SHOULD send PUSH_PROMISE (Section 6.6) frames prior to
   sending any frames that reference the promised responses.  This
   avoids a race where clients issue requests prior to receiving any
   PUSH_PROMISE frames.
requirements.condition: When a server will send both a PUSH_PROMISE and frames that reference the promised response.
requirements.required_behavior: The server should send the PUSH_PROMISE before any frame that references the promised response.
requirements.why_checkable: The transmitted frame sequence can be checked for the prescribed ordering.

requirements.quote: PUSH_PROMISE frames MUST NOT be sent by the client.
requirements.condition: For a client endpoint.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: The client must not send PUSH_PROMISE frames.
requirements.why_checkable: Outbound client frames can be observed for any PUSH_PROMISE frame.

requirements.quote:
PUSH_PROMISE frames can be sent by the server on any client-initiated
   stream, but the stream MUST be in either the "open" or "half-closed
   (remote)" state with respect to the server.  PUSH_PROMISE frames are
   interspersed with the frames that comprise a response, though they
   cannot be interspersed with HEADERS and CONTINUATION frames that
   comprise a single field block.
requirements.condition: When a server sends a PUSH_PROMISE frame on a stream.
requirements.required_behavior: The target stream must be client-initiated.
requirements.why_checkable: The initiator of the stream carrying the PUSH_PROMISE is observable from the stream identifier and connection role.

requirements.quote:
PUSH_PROMISE frames can be sent by the server on any client-initiated
   stream, but the stream MUST be in either the "open" or "half-closed
   (remote)" state with respect to the server.  PUSH_PROMISE frames are
   interspersed with the frames that comprise a response, though they
   cannot be interspersed with HEADERS and CONTINUATION frames that
   comprise a single field block.
requirements.condition: When a server sends a PUSH_PROMISE frame on a client-initiated stream.
requirements.required_behavior: The stream must be in the "open" or "half-closed (remote)" state with respect to the server.
requirements.why_checkable: The stream state at the instant the PUSH_PROMISE is sent can be tracked and compared with the two allowed states.

requirements.quote:
PUSH_PROMISE frames can be sent by the server on any client-initiated
   stream, but the stream MUST be in either the "open" or "half-closed
   (remote)" state with respect to the server.  PUSH_PROMISE frames are
   interspersed with the frames that comprise a response, though they
   cannot be interspersed with HEADERS and CONTINUATION frames that
   comprise a single field block.
requirements.condition: While HEADERS and CONTINUATION frames are carrying one field block.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: A PUSH_PROMISE frame cannot be interspersed within that HEADERS/CONTINUATION sequence.
requirements.why_checkable: Frame ordering can be inspected to detect a PUSH_PROMISE inserted before the field block terminates.

requirements.quote:
Sending a PUSH_PROMISE frame creates a new stream and puts the stream
   into the "reserved (local)" state for the server and the "reserved
   (remote)" state for the client.
requirements.condition: When a server sends a PUSH_PROMISE frame.
requirements.required_behavior: A new promised stream is created in the "reserved (local)" state for the server.
requirements.why_checkable: The server-side promised-stream state immediately after sending PUSH_PROMISE can be inspected.

requirements.quote:
Sending a PUSH_PROMISE frame creates a new stream and puts the stream
   into the "reserved (local)" state for the server and the "reserved
   (remote)" state for the client.
requirements.condition: When a client receives a PUSH_PROMISE frame.
requirements.required_behavior: A new promised stream is created in the "reserved (remote)" state for the client.
requirements.why_checkable: The client-side promised-stream state immediately after receiving PUSH_PROMISE can be inspected.

requirements.quote:
After sending the PUSH_PROMISE frame, the server can begin delivering
   the pushed response as a response (Section 8.3.2) on a server-
   initiated stream that uses the promised stream identifier.  The
   server uses this stream to transmit an HTTP response, using the same
   sequence of frames as that defined in Section 8.1.  This stream
   becomes "half-closed" to the client (Section 5.1) after the initial
   HEADERS frame is sent.
requirements.condition: When a server delivers a pushed response after PUSH_PROMISE.
requirements.required_behavior: The pushed response must be delivered on a server-initiated stream using the promised stream identifier.
requirements.why_checkable: The response stream's initiator and identifier can be compared with the preceding PUSH_PROMISE.

requirements.quote:
After sending the PUSH_PROMISE frame, the server can begin delivering
   the pushed response as a response (Section 8.3.2) on a server-
   initiated stream that uses the promised stream identifier.  The
   server uses this stream to transmit an HTTP response, using the same
   sequence of frames as that defined in Section 8.1.  This stream
   becomes "half-closed" to the client (Section 5.1) after the initial
   HEADERS frame is sent.
requirements.condition: When a server transmits an HTTP pushed response on the promised stream.
requirements.required_behavior: The server uses the response frame sequence defined in Section 8.1.
requirements.why_checkable: The pushed response's frame sequence can be observed and compared with the referenced response sequence.

requirements.quote:
After sending the PUSH_PROMISE frame, the server can begin delivering
   the pushed response as a response (Section 8.3.2) on a server-
   initiated stream that uses the promised stream identifier.  The
   server uses this stream to transmit an HTTP response, using the same
   sequence of frames as that defined in Section 8.1.  This stream
   becomes "half-closed" to the client (Section 5.1) after the initial
   HEADERS frame is sent.
requirements.condition: After the initial HEADERS frame of a pushed response is sent.
requirements.required_behavior: The promised stream becomes "half-closed" to the client.
requirements.why_checkable: The client-side stream state can be inspected immediately after the initial HEADERS frame.

requirements.quote:
Once a client receives a PUSH_PROMISE frame and chooses to accept the
   pushed response, the client SHOULD NOT issue any requests for the
   promised response until after the promised stream has closed.
requirements.condition: After a client receives a PUSH_PROMISE and accepts the pushed response, until the promised stream closes.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: The client should not issue a request for the promised response.
requirements.why_checkable: Client requests can be monitored between acceptance of the PUSH_PROMISE and closure of the promised stream.

requirements.quote:
If the client determines, for any reason, that it does not wish to
   receive the pushed response from the server or if the server takes
   too long to begin sending the promised response, the client can send
   a RST_STREAM frame, using either the CANCEL or REFUSED_STREAM code
   and referencing the pushed stream's identifier.
requirements.condition: If a client rejects a pushed response or determines that the server took too long to begin it, and the client sends RST_STREAM.
requirements.required_behavior: The RST_STREAM frame uses either the CANCEL or REFUSED_STREAM code and references the pushed stream's identifier.
requirements.why_checkable: The reset frame's error code and stream identifier can be inspected.

requirements.quote:
A client can use the SETTINGS_MAX_CONCURRENT_STREAMS setting to limit
   the number of responses that can be concurrently pushed by a server.
   Advertising a SETTINGS_MAX_CONCURRENT_STREAMS value of zero prevents
   the server from opening the streams necessary to push responses.
   However, this does not prevent the server from reserving streams
   using PUSH_PROMISE frames, because reserved streams do not count
   toward the concurrent stream limit.  Clients that do not wish to
   receive pushed resources need to reset any unwanted reserved streams
   or set SETTINGS_ENABLE_PUSH to 0.
requirements.condition: When a client advertises SETTINGS_MAX_CONCURRENT_STREAMS with a value of zero.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: The server cannot open streams necessary to push responses.
requirements.why_checkable: After the zero setting is advertised, attempts by the server to open pushed-response streams can be observed.

requirements.quote:
A client can use the SETTINGS_MAX_CONCURRENT_STREAMS setting to limit
   the number of responses that can be concurrently pushed by a server.
   Advertising a SETTINGS_MAX_CONCURRENT_STREAMS value of zero prevents
   the server from opening the streams necessary to push responses.
   However, this does not prevent the server from reserving streams
   using PUSH_PROMISE frames, because reserved streams do not count
   toward the concurrent stream limit.  Clients that do not wish to
   receive pushed resources need to reset any unwanted reserved streams
   or set SETTINGS_ENABLE_PUSH to 0.
requirements.condition: When enforcing the concurrent stream limit.
requirements.required_behavior: Reserved streams are excluded from the concurrent stream count.
requirements.why_checkable: The implementation's concurrent-stream accounting can be tested with reserved promised streams present.

requirements.quote:
A client can use the SETTINGS_MAX_CONCURRENT_STREAMS setting to limit
   the number of responses that can be concurrently pushed by a server.
   Advertising a SETTINGS_MAX_CONCURRENT_STREAMS value of zero prevents
   the server from opening the streams necessary to push responses.
   However, this does not prevent the server from reserving streams
   using PUSH_PROMISE frames, because reserved streams do not count
   toward the concurrent stream limit.  Clients that do not wish to
   receive pushed resources need to reset any unwanted reserved streams
   or set SETTINGS_ENABLE_PUSH to 0.
requirements.condition: When a client does not wish to receive pushed resources.
requirements.required_behavior: The client needs to reset unwanted reserved streams or set SETTINGS_ENABLE_PUSH to 0.
requirements.why_checkable: Client settings and handling of unwanted reserved streams can be observed.

requirements.quote:
Clients receiving a pushed response MUST validate that either the
   server is authoritative (see Section 10.1) or the proxy that provided
   the pushed response is configured for the corresponding request.  For
   example, a server that offers a certificate for only the example.com
   DNS-ID (see [RFC6125]) is not permitted to push a response for
   <https://www.example.org/doc>.
requirements.condition: When a client receives a pushed response directly from a server.
requirements.required_behavior: The client must validate that the server is authoritative for the pushed response.
requirements.why_checkable: The pushed response's origin can be compared with the server's established authority.

requirements.quote:
Clients receiving a pushed response MUST validate that either the
   server is authoritative (see Section 10.1) or the proxy that provided
   the pushed response is configured for the corresponding request.  For
   example, a server that offers a certificate for only the example.com
   DNS-ID (see [RFC6125]) is not permitted to push a response for
   <https://www.example.org/doc>.
requirements.condition: When a client receives a pushed response from a proxy.
requirements.required_behavior: The client must validate that the proxy is configured for the corresponding request.
requirements.why_checkable: Proxy configuration and the corresponding pushed request can be compared during response validation.

requirements.quote:
The response for a PUSH_PROMISE stream begins with a HEADERS frame,
   which immediately puts the stream into the "half-closed (remote)"
   state for the server and "half-closed (local)" state for the client,
   and ends with a frame with the END_STREAM flag set, which places the
   stream in the "closed" state.
requirements.condition: When a response begins on a PUSH_PROMISE stream.
requirements.required_behavior: The first response frame must be a HEADERS frame.
requirements.why_checkable: The first frame of the pushed response can be inspected for type HEADERS.

requirements.quote:
The response for a PUSH_PROMISE stream begins with a HEADERS frame,
   which immediately puts the stream into the "half-closed (remote)"
   state for the server and "half-closed (local)" state for the client,
   and ends with a frame with the END_STREAM flag set, which places the
   stream in the "closed" state.
requirements.condition: Immediately after the initial HEADERS frame of a PUSH_PROMISE response.
requirements.required_behavior: The stream enters the "half-closed (remote)" state for the server.
requirements.why_checkable: The server-side stream state can be inspected after the initial HEADERS frame.

requirements.quote:
The response for a PUSH_PROMISE stream begins with a HEADERS frame,
   which immediately puts the stream into the "half-closed (remote)"
   state for the server and "half-closed (local)" state for the client,
   and ends with a frame with the END_STREAM flag set, which places the
   stream in the "closed" state.
requirements.condition: Immediately after the initial HEADERS frame of a PUSH_PROMISE response.
requirements.required_behavior: The stream enters the "half-closed (local)" state for the client.
requirements.why_checkable: The client-side stream state can be inspected after the initial HEADERS frame.

requirements.quote:
The response for a PUSH_PROMISE stream begins with a HEADERS frame,
   which immediately puts the stream into the "half-closed (remote)"
   state for the server and "half-closed (local)" state for the client,
   and ends with a frame with the END_STREAM flag set, which places the
   stream in the "closed" state.
requirements.condition: When a response on a PUSH_PROMISE stream ends.
requirements.required_behavior: Its final frame must have the END_STREAM flag set.
requirements.why_checkable: The terminal response frame can be inspected for the END_STREAM flag.

requirements.quote:
The response for a PUSH_PROMISE stream begins with a HEADERS frame,
   which immediately puts the stream into the "half-closed (remote)"
   state for the server and "half-closed (local)" state for the client,
   and ends with a frame with the END_STREAM flag set, which places the
   stream in the "closed" state.
requirements.condition: When a frame with END_STREAM set ends the response on a PUSH_PROMISE stream.
requirements.required_behavior: The stream enters the "closed" state.
requirements.why_checkable: The stream state can be inspected immediately after processing the terminal END_STREAM frame.

requirements.quote:
|  Note: The client never sends a frame with the END_STREAM flag
      |  set for a server push.
requirements.condition: For a server-push stream.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: The client must never send a frame with the END_STREAM flag set.
requirements.why_checkable: All client-originated frames on server-push streams can be inspected for END_STREAM.

requirements.quote:
In HTTP/2, the CONNECT method establishes a tunnel over a single
   HTTP/2 stream to a remote host, rather than converting the entire
   connection to a tunnel.  A CONNECT header section is constructed as
   defined in Section 8.3.1 ("Request Pseudo-Header Fields"), with a few
   differences.  Specifically:
requirements.condition: When HTTP/2 CONNECT establishes a tunnel.
requirements.required_behavior: The tunnel is established over a single HTTP/2 stream.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: CONNECT must not convert the entire HTTP/2 connection into the tunnel.
requirements.why_checkable: Traffic and stream allocation can be observed to verify that the tunnel is confined to one stream.

requirements.quote: *  The ":method" pseudo-header field is set to CONNECT.
requirements.condition: When constructing a CONNECT request header section.
requirements.required_behavior: The ":method" pseudo-header field must be set to CONNECT.
requirements.why_checkable: The CONNECT header section can be decoded and its ":method" value compared with CONNECT.

requirements.quote: *  The ":scheme" and ":path" pseudo-header fields MUST be omitted.
requirements.condition: When constructing a CONNECT request header section.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: The ":scheme" pseudo-header field must not be included.
requirements.why_checkable: The decoded CONNECT header section can be checked for absence of ":scheme".

requirements.quote: *  The ":scheme" and ":path" pseudo-header fields MUST be omitted.
requirements.condition: When constructing a CONNECT request header section.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: The ":path" pseudo-header field must not be included.
requirements.why_checkable: The decoded CONNECT header section can be checked for absence of ":path".

requirements.quote:
*  The ":authority" pseudo-header field contains the host and port to
      connect to (equivalent to the authority-form of the request-target
      of CONNECT requests; see Section 3.2.3 of [HTTP/1.1]).
requirements.condition: When constructing a CONNECT request header section.
requirements.required_behavior: The ":authority" pseudo-header field must contain the host and port to which the tunnel will connect.
requirements.why_checkable: The decoded ":authority" value can be checked for the requested host and port.

requirements.quote:
A CONNECT request that does not conform to these restrictions is
   malformed (Section 8.1.1).
requirements.condition: If a CONNECT request violates the stated CONNECT header-section restrictions.
requirements.error_behavior: The request must be classified and handled as malformed.
requirements.why_checkable: Nonconforming CONNECT header sections can be supplied and the implementation's malformed-request classification observed.

requirements.quote:
A proxy that supports CONNECT establishes a TCP connection [TCP] to
   the host and port identified in the ":authority" pseudo-header field.
   Once this connection is successfully established, the proxy sends a
   HEADERS frame containing a 2xx-series status code to the client, as
   defined in Section 9.3.6 of [HTTP].
requirements.condition: When a CONNECT-supporting proxy processes a conforming CONNECT request.
requirements.required_behavior: The proxy establishes a TCP connection to the host and port identified by the ":authority" pseudo-header field.
requirements.why_checkable: The proxy's outbound TCP connection target can be compared with the received ":authority" value.

requirements.quote:
A proxy that supports CONNECT establishes a TCP connection [TCP] to
   the host and port identified in the ":authority" pseudo-header field.
   Once this connection is successfully established, the proxy sends a
   HEADERS frame containing a 2xx-series status code to the client, as
   defined in Section 9.3.6 of [HTTP].
requirements.condition: Once the proxy successfully establishes the requested TCP connection.
requirements.required_behavior: The proxy sends a HEADERS frame to the client.
requirements.why_checkable: The proxy's frames after successful TCP establishment can be observed for a HEADERS frame.

requirements.quote:
A proxy that supports CONNECT establishes a TCP connection [TCP] to
   the host and port identified in the ":authority" pseudo-header field.
   Once this connection is successfully established, the proxy sends a
   HEADERS frame containing a 2xx-series status code to the client, as
   defined in Section 9.3.6 of [HTTP].
requirements.condition: When the proxy sends the HEADERS frame after successfully establishing the requested TCP connection.
requirements.required_behavior: The HEADERS frame must contain a 2xx-series status code.
requirements.why_checkable: The response header block can be decoded and its status code checked to be in the 2xx range.
